batches.about: A Kotlin Android app for planning bird-watching trips: Compose UI, feature modules, a benchmark module.

statements.text: Tern is an Android app for planning bird-watching trips: sightings, routes and checklists, offline first.
Build a debug APK with `./gradlew assembleDebug`.
Install it on a connected device with `./gradlew installDebug`.
The project builds with JDK 17.
minSdk is 26; targetSdk and compileSdk are 35.
Kotlin 2.1, with the Compose compiler Gradle plugin.
Run the unit tests with `./gradlew test` before every commit.
Instrumented tests live in `app/src/androidTest` and run on an emulator or a device.
Test Flows with Turbine.
Screenshot tests use Roborazzi; record new baselines with `./gradlew recordRoborazziDebug`.
The app is a single activity with Jetpack Compose screens and Navigation Compose.
Use Hilt for dependency injection.
Each feature is a Gradle module under `feature/`, and features never depend on each other.
Repositories expose `Flow`s; ViewModels collect them into a `StateFlow` of UI state.
Disk and network calls run off the main thread, on `Dispatchers.IO`.
Room is the only local database; migrations are tested with `MigrationTestHelper`.
Use Gradle's Kotlin DSL (`build.gradle.kts`) for every module.
Run `./gradlew ktlintCheck` before pushing.
Prefer `sealed interface` over `sealed class` for UI state.
Keep files under 400 lines.
Run the macrobenchmarks with `./gradlew :benchmark:connectedCheck` on a physical device only; emulator numbers are meaningless.
Baseline profiles are regenerated before each release.
`./gradlew assembleDebug` builds the debug APK; `./gradlew bundleRelease` builds the release bundle.
Use JDK 21 to build; the Gradle toolchain is set to 21.
Lint with `./gradlew ktlintCheck detekt`.
Composable function names start with a lowercase verb, like `showProfile()`.
Dependency injection is done with Koin; modules are declared in `di/`.
Never block the main thread: do disk and network work in a coroutine on `Dispatchers.IO`.
Strings shown to people go in `res/values/strings.xml`, never inline.
Use `kotlinx.serialization` for JSON, not Gson or Moshi.
Keep composables under 60 lines; split larger ones into private composables.
The code relies on the K2 compiler, so Kotlin 2.0 or later.
Release builds are signed in CI; never commit the keystore.
The Play Store release train ships every other Tuesday.
Release branches are cut on the Monday before a release train.
Name composables in PascalCase, as nouns: `ProfileCard`, not `showProfile`.
Every screen-level composable takes its state and event callbacks as parameters, with no ViewModel inside.
Hoist state; use `remember` only for state that belongs to the UI alone.
Previews go in the same file, annotated `@PreviewLightDark`.
Use Material 3 components from `androidx.compose.material3`.
The app supports Android 7.0 (API 24) and later.
Don't run the Gradle test task locally; CI runs the unit tests on every push.
Don't use a DI framework; pass dependencies through constructors.
New modules use Groovy `build.gradle` files, like the existing `app` module.
Serialize every JSON payload with `kotlinx.serialization`.
Write KDoc for every public function in `core/`.
Network calls go through the Retrofit services in `core/network`.
Images load with Coil.

batches.about: A shipping-rates platform: a Go API, a Next.js dashboard and the Terraform for both.

statements.text: Harbor runs the shipping-rates platform: a Go API in `api/`, a Next.js dashboard in `web/` and the Terraform for both in `infra/`.
Install Go 1.23, Node 22 and Terraform 1.9.
Copy `.env.example` to `.env`; never commit `.env`.
`make dev` starts the API, the dashboard and a local Postgres in Docker.
Lint Go with `golangci-lint run ./...`.
Run the API tests with `go test ./...`; they need Docker for Postgres.
Errors use RFC 9457 problem details (`application/problem+json`).
Handlers take a `context.Context` first, and never both log and return the same error.
Database access goes through `sqlc`-generated queries in `api/internal/db`; no hand-written SQL in handlers.
Format Go with `gofmt`, which indents with tabs.
In `web/`, use npm; the lockfile is `package-lock.json`.
Run the dashboard's tests with `npm test` inside `web/`.
Server components by default; add `"use client"` only for interactivity.
Production applies run from `main` after the merge, through the `apply` workflow.
Every change gets a `terraform plan` in the pull request.
State lives in the S3 backend with DynamoDB locking; state files never go into git.
Keep pull requests under 400 changed lines.
Squash-merge; the pull request's title becomes the commit message.
`make dev` runs everything locally.
`make test` runs the Go tests and the dashboard tests.
API errors are returned as `{"error": {"code": "...", "message": "..."}}` with a matching HTTP status.
Go code is linted with `staticcheck` only; golangci-lint was removed in 2025.
Use `slog` for logging, with the request ID on every line.
Write table-driven tests, with `t.Run` per case.
`go.mod` says `go 1.23.4`, with the toolchain line removed.
The change freeze for the Q4 network migration starts on November 20.
Never commit `.tfstate` files.
Every module has a README listing its inputs and outputs.
Lambda timeouts are at most 25 seconds.
Pin Terraform to 1.6.x; newer versions change the provider lock format we rely on.
Run `terraform fmt -recursive` before committing.
Generate module docs with `terraform-docs markdown table`.
Never use `count` for resources with an identity of their own; use `for_each`.
Tag every resource with `team`, `service` and `env`.
Since February 2026 every resource lives in `vpc-main`.
Install packages with `bun add`; bun is the dashboard's package manager.
Use 2-space indentation and double quotes.
Fetch data in server components with `fetch` and `next: { revalidate }`.
Use the design tokens in `web/styles/tokens.css`; no raw hex colours.
Format with Prettier before committing.
Only the `prod` branch triggers production applies; `main` applies to staging.
No infrastructure changes after November 15 until the network migration is done.
The legacy VPC (`vpc-legacy`) was retired on 2026-02-01; don't reference it.
API Gateway times out after 29 seconds.
Ask before running `terraform apply` against anything but a sandbox account.
